guidelineVersions: GMC Intimate examinations and chaperones (updated December 2024)

related.why: Gloving and keeping a sterile field
Another bedside procedure with consent and aseptic technique

brief.setting: Surgical ward, on a male catheterisation manikin
brief.scenario: Mr Owen Bartley, 74, had an open inguinal hernia repair this morning. He hasn't passed urine for 9 hours and has lower abdominal discomfort. A bladder scan shows 850 ml. He is uncircumcised. A catheter pack, anaesthetic gel, catheters and a drainage bag are provided.
brief.task: Catheterise the manikin, talking the examiner through each step, and answer questions.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Indication, consent and chaperone; aseptic, gel and wait; urine before the balloon; foreskin back; closed system; document.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Inflating the balloon before urine flows, or leaving the foreskin retracted.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "I'll explain why he needs a catheter, get his consent and offer a chaperone."

grid.label: Indication, consent and chaperone
grid.fail: Starts without explaining, gaining consent or offering a chaperone.
grid.pass: Confirms the indication (acute retention), explains the procedure, gains consent and offers a chaperone.
grid.high: Records the chaperone discussion and who was present; checks he knows the catheter will come out as soon as possible.

grid.label: Allergies and equipment
grid.fail: Doesn't ask about latex, lidocaine or chlorhexidine allergy.
grid.pass: Asks about latex, lidocaine and chlorhexidine allergy; chooses the smallest catheter that will drain, with a 10 ml balloon.
grid.high: Knows the anaesthetic gel contains chlorhexidine and lidocaine, and isn't used on bleeding or damaged urethral mucosa.

grid.label: Aseptic technique
grid.fail: Touches the catheter tip or the glans with a contaminated glove.
grid.pass: Hand hygiene, sterile field and gloves; retracts the foreskin with a swab; cleans the meatus with sterile saline.
grid.high: Keeps a non-touch technique throughout, and changes to a second pair of sterile gloves after the gel.

grid.label: Anaesthetic gel
grid.fail: Uses no gel, or dry lubricant only.
grid.borderline: Instils the gel but starts inserting straight away.
grid.pass: Instils 11 ml of lidocaine gel from a sterile single-use syringe, squeezes the glans and waits about 3–5 minutes.
grid.high: Explains the wait lets the anaesthetic act and the gel lubricates the whole urethra; follows the manufacturer's timing.

grid.label: Insertion and balloon
grid.fail: Inflates the balloon before urine flows, or pushes on against pain.
grid.pass: Penis at 90 degrees; inserts until urine flows, then 2–5 cm further; inflates slowly with sterile water per the manufacturer; stops if painful.
grid.high: Asks him to cough or strain gently if resisted at the sphincter; after inflating, withdraws slightly to check it is secure; never inflates without urine.

grid.label: Foreskin replaced (safety-critical)
grid.pass: Cleans the glans and returns the foreskin over it.
grid.high: Explains a retracted foreskin can cause paraphimosis, a urological emergency that can lead to gangrene.

grid.label: Closed drainage and documentation
grid.fail: Leaves an open or disconnected system, or doesn't record anything.
grid.pass: Connects a sterile closed system, bag below the bladder; records residual volume, catheter type, size, batch and expiry, and balloon water.
grid.high: Records the indication and removal plan, and plans a trial without catheter.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Starts opening the pack without explaining or asking about a chaperone.]

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Touches the catheter tip with the glove used to hold the penis.]

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Squirts a little lubricant on the tip; no anaesthetic gel.]

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Pushes the catheter in partway and inflates the balloon before any urine appears.]

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Leaves the bag on the bed; writes nothing down.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Mr Bartley, your bladder is holding 850 ml and you can't pass urine, so I'd like to put in a catheter. May I? Would you like a chaperone?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Any allergy to latex, local anaesthetic or chlorhexidine? I'll use the smallest catheter that will drain, with a 10 ml balloon.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Hand hygiene, sterile gloves and field; retracts the foreskin with a swab; cleans the meatus with sterile saline.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Instils 11 ml of anaesthetic gel, squeezes the glans.] I'll wait 3 to 5 minutes for it to work.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Holds the penis at 90 degrees, inserts until urine flows, then 2 to 5 cm further; inflates slowly with sterile water.] Tell me if it hurts.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Cleans the glans and returns the foreskin.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Connects a sterile closed bag, hung below the bladder.] I'll record 900 ml drained, the catheter type, size, batch and expiry, and the balloon volume.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Your bladder is holding 850 ml after the operation, which is why it's uncomfortable. A catheter will drain it; I'll aim to remove it as soon as possible. Are you happy for me to go ahead? Would you like a chaperone? [Records the chaperone discussion and who is present.]

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Any allergy to latex, lidocaine or chlorhexidine? This gel contains both, and I wouldn't use it if the urethra were bleeding. Smallest catheter that will drain, 10 ml balloon.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Non-touch technique throughout: retracts the foreskin with a swab, cleans the meatus with saline, touches only the catheter sleeve.]

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Instils all 11 ml, squeezes the glans.] Waiting 3 to 5 minutes lets it numb and lubricate the whole urethra. [Changes to fresh sterile gloves.]

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Penis at 90 degrees; resistance at the sphincter, so asks him to cough; urine flows, then advances 2 to 5 cm further; inflates slowly with sterile water to the manufacturer's volume; withdraws slightly.] No pain? Good.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Cleans the glans, returns the foreskin.] Leaving it back risks paraphimosis, which can compromise the glans.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Closed system, bag below the bladder, off the floor.] I'll record 900 ml residual, indication, catheter details with the sticker, balloon volume, and a plan for a trial without catheter.

failures.move: Leaving the foreskin retracted after catheterisation.
failures.consequence: Safety-critical: paraphimosis, which can progress to ischaemia of the glans.

failures.move: Inflating the balloon before urine flows.
failures.consequence: Safety-critical: inflating in the prostatic urethra causes pain, bleeding and urethral trauma.

failures.move: Contaminating the catheter tip or glans.
failures.consequence: Introduces bacteria into the bladder: catheter-associated infection.

failures.move: No chaperone offered, or not recorded.
failures.consequence: Breaches GMC guidance for an intimate procedure.

recovery.line: I won't inflate. I'll check the position, press gently over the bladder, and if still nothing, remove and reassess.
Before I finish, I'll return his foreskin to prevent paraphimosis.

knowledge.fact: Catheterisation is aseptic; clean the meatus with sterile saline; lubricant from a sterile single-use container.
Smallest gauge that drains; 10 ml balloon in adults.
Sterile closed drainage with a sampling port; bag below the bladder, off the floor.
Anaesthetic gel: instil 11 ml and wait about 3–5 minutes; when urine flows, advance a further 2–5 cm; then inflate slowly.
Instillagel contains lidocaine and chlorhexidine; avoid with hypersensitivity or bleeding mucosa.

recall.say: "Urine first, then the balloon; foreskin back before I finish."
recall.trap: Inflating as soon as the catheter feels in.
recall.finish: Closed system, residual and catheter details recorded, removal plan.

sources.name: Loveday HP, Wilson JA, Pratt RJ, et al. epic3: national evidence-based guidelines for preventing healthcare-associated infections in NHS hospitals in England. J Hosp Infect 2014;86(Suppl 1):S1-S70
sources.supports: Short-term urethral catheters: only when clinically indicated, after alternatives and discussion (UC1); document indication, date, type, drainage system and removal plan (UC2); assess latex allergy (UC4); smallest gauge that allows outflow and a 10 ml balloon in adults (UC6); aseptic procedure by trained staff (UC7); clean the meatus with sterile saline (UC8); lubricant from a sterile single-use container (UC9); sterile closed drainage system with a sampling port (UC10); don't break the connection (UC11); bag below the bladder, off the floor (UC15)

sources.name: Royal College of Nursing: Catheter care: RCN guidance for health care professionals (publication code 010 988)
sources.supports: Male procedure (appendix 3): discuss a chaperone and gain consent; retract the foreskin with a sterile swab, clean the meatus with sterile saline; penis at 90 degrees; insert all 11 ml of anaesthetic gel, squeeze and wait approximately 3 to 5 minutes according to the manufacturer's instructions; change to a second pair of sterile gloves; insert 15 cm to 25 cm; if resistance is felt at the external sphincter, ask the patient to cough or strain gently; when urine begins to flow, advance a further 2 cm to 5 cm; inflate the balloon slowly per the manufacturer, stopping and rechecking the position if there is discomfort, then withdraw slightly and check it remains secure; clean the glans and reduce the foreskin; measure urine drained; document reason, consent, catheter manufacturer, material, batch and expiry, size and length, gel, balloon water volume and drainage system; paraphimosis is a urological emergency that can result in gangrene; allergy risks include latex and lidocaine gels

sources.name: Instillagel (lidocaine hydrochloride and chlorhexidine gluconate gel): UK Summary of Product Characteristics (Farco-Pharma)
sources.supports: Catheterisation: instil 6-11 ml, press the glans until the anaesthetic effect begins; for cystoscopy the effect begins after 3.5 minutes; contraindicated with hypersensitivity to amide anaesthetics, chlorhexidine or hydroxybenzoates, and with damaged or bleeding mucosa

partner.opening: Please catheterise Mr Bartley using this manikin, talking me through what you're doing.

reveals.trigger: Asks about consent and a chaperone
reveals.finding: He agrees and would like a chaperone; a nurse is available.
No allergies. No bleeding from the urethra.
Say: "You feel resistance about 16 cm in."

push.question: Why wait after the gel?
push.expect: It needs about 3–5 minutes to anaesthetise; follow the manufacturer's timing.

push.question: When do you inflate the balloon?
push.expect: Only after urine flows and the catheter is advanced further; slowly, stopping if painful.

push.question: What must you do before you leave?
push.expect: Return the foreskin to prevent paraphimosis.

curveballs.prompt: He says it hurts as you start inflating.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Stop, deflate, and advance further or reposition before trying again.

curveballs.prompt: You can't pass the catheter beyond the prostate after two gentle attempts.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Stop; don't force it. Call the senior or urology team.

curveballs.prompt: He tells you he reacted to chlorhexidine at the dentist.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Don't use chlorhexidine-containing gel: use a sterile lubricant or anaesthetic gel without it.
